reliability: Primary agency description of its workflow/rule; reliable within stated scope, not independent customer-demand evidence. HTTP 200 public HTML read on access date.
findings: CMS describes the rule as reducing prior-authorization burden and requires specified impacted payers to implement APIs for requirements discovery, requests and responses.
The fact sheet describes operational compliance generally beginning January 1, 2026 and API compliance generally beginning January 1, 2027, with exact dates varying by payer.
The described prior-authorization provisions exclude drugs; the impacted payer list is limited rather than all US insurance.
CMS specifies denial reasons and, for impacted payers excluding QHP issuers on FFEs, 72-hour expedited and seven-calendar-day standard decision timeframes.
limitations: A rule fact sheet, not an empirical survey of small medical practices or proof that requirements have been implemented by each payer.
No later-rule or litigation search was completed; treat dates as the fact sheet's description and verify current implementation before recommending a product.
All claims drawn from this page are one CMS evidence stream, not independent confirmations.
